title: BlazeLIMS Pricing: One-Time vs SaaS Costs, Reviews and Alternatives
summary: BlazeLIMS pricing from Blaze Systems' own price list: one-time licence vs SaaS, the 18% annual support fee, a five-year cost example, reviews and alternatives.
body_markdown:
### TL;DR


- Blaze Systems publishes BlazeLIMS prices, which is rare for a LIMS. A one-time licence starts at $10,575 for 3 concurrent users.
- SaaS starts at $600 a month for 2 concurrent users, with no contract and 30 days' notice.
- One-time licences add 18% a year for support. For 5 users over five years, list prices come to about $34,200 one-time versus $54,000 for SaaS.
- Implementation, validation, servers and IT time aren't on the list, so get them quoted in writing.

Unlike most LIMS vendors, Blaze Systems publishes its prices. The harder question is which model to choose: a one-time licence with yearly support, or a monthly subscription. This guide covers the published prices, a five-year example, what the list leaves out, reviews and alternatives. For the wider market, see our[LIMS pricing guide](https://www.scispot.com/blog/understanding-lims-pricing-how-much-does-a-lims-cost) .


## How BlazeLIMS Pricing Works


BlazeLIMS is sold two ways, both priced by concurrent users (people logged in at the same time). These figures come from Blaze's price page, checked on 31 Oct 2026.


### One-Time (Site-Hosted) Licence


- BlazeLIMS: $10,575 for 3 concurrent users or $17,995 for 5. Extra users cost $3,525 each (users 6–10), $2,100 (11–20) and $700 above 20.
- BlazeInventory, which includes an ELN, and BlazeStability: $8,825 each as add-ons, or $10,700 each standalone.
- BlazeLink instrument interfacing: $900 per instrument.
- Annual support: 18% of the licence value.


### SaaS Subscription


- BlazeLIMS: $600 a month for 2 concurrent users, plus $100 a month for each additional user.
- BlazeInventory is included. BlazeStability is a $300-a-month add-on.
- BlazeLink: $900 per instrument.
- No contract, and 30 days' cancellation notice.


Blaze's SaaS page also offers a free 60-day trial with two hours of web training, and caps annual hotline support at 15 incidents for 1–5 users, with extra incidents at $200 each.


### Why Blaze's Own Pages Show Different Numbers


Blaze's home page lists "typical" pricing of $12,000 one-time or $512 a month for 3 users, and its pharma page repeats those figures. The SaaS page lists 1 user at $350 a month and 10 users at $1,400. The price page is the most detailed, so this guide uses it. Ask for a written quote that says which list it's based on.


## What BlazeLIMS Costs Over Five Years


Here's a simple example for a lab with 5 concurrent users and BlazeLIMS only, using Blaze's list prices. It assumes support is paid every year, including the first.


- One-time licence: $17,995 up front plus $3,239.10 a year in support (18%), or about $34,190 over five years.
- SaaS: $900 a month ($600 for 2 users plus 3 × $100), or $54,000 over five years.


On paper the one-time licence wins, as Blaze's own site says, but you run the server, database and backups. SaaS costs more over five years but starts lower, includes BlazeInventory (an $8,825 add-on on the one-time model) and can be cancelled with 30 days' notice. Add $900 for each instrument you connect, on either model.


### What the Price List Doesn't Cover


- Implementation and configuration of your tests, specs and reports.
- Data migration. Blaze mentions a legacy data migration wizard and support, but not a price.
- Validation, if you work under GMP, GLP or 21 CFR Part 11.
- Training beyond the trial session, and support beyond your incident allowance.
- For site-hosted installs, servers, database licences, backups and IT staff time.

## BlazeLIMS Reviews and Alternatives


### What Reviews Say


User reviews are scarce. GetApp shows no reviews for BlazeLIMS, and CrowdReviews shows none. ITQlick scores it 55 out of 100 and itechguides gives an editor score of 6.0 out of 10, but these are editorial ratings, not customer feedback. Ask for references from a lab like yours, and use the free trial to test your workflows.


### Alternatives by Lab Type


- Small testing labs that want published prices: QBench and CloudLIMS.
- Regulated enterprise labs: LabWare, STARLIMS and LabVantage.
- Environmental and public-sector labs: Sample Master.
- Life science and diagnostics labs scaling up: platforms priced without seat fees, such as Scispot (below).


Whatever you shortlist, score each option with our[LIMS vendor selection framework](https://www.scispot.com/blog/the-complete-guide-to-lims-vendor-selection-a-data-driven-evaluation-framework-for-lab-leaders) .
